PullRequest.Title: sessions: add Manage Remotes link to automation warnings
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- Add a localized **Manage Remotes** link after the disconnected-remotes banner message, opening the existing Remote Environments editor in the Agents window. Also provide the entry point in the unavailable empty state.
- Respect the existing remote-management settings, preserve unavailable-provider messages, support pointer/Enter/Space activation, and report command failures.
- Update accessibility help and add component screenshot coverage for single/multiple disconnected hosts, narrow layouts, and high contrast.

## Validation

- **Passed:** seven focused production tests via a source-based Vite/browser Mocha harness, covering command routing, settings changes, provider states, failure reporting, existing unavailable messages, and accessibility help. The standard unit runners could not load the generated test module in this environment.
- **Passed:** seven component screenshot variants, visually inspected, with identical image hashes across two independent renders. Rendering used a temporary Vite configuration to accommodate missing development dependencies; it is not included in the change.
- **Passed:** changed-file ESLint:
  ```sh
  node --max-old-space-size=8192 build/eslint.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/automationsView.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/automationsAccessibility.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/automationsView.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/automationsView.fixture.ts
  ```
- **Passed:** Stylelint, with existing design-token suggestions:
  ```sh
  node build/stylelint.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/media/automationsCards.css
  ```
- **Blocked:** standard client compilation because pnpm was unavailable and fallback build attempts encountered missing `gulp-merge-json`/`esbuild` dependencies.
- **Failed on existing dependency/type diagnostics:** `node_modules/.bin/tsc --project src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck`. No diagnostics were reported for the changed files.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open Automations with one or more disconnected remote providers and saved automations. Click **Manage Remotes** after the warning text and confirm that Remote Environments opens. Repeat without saved automations.
2. Activate the link using Enter or Space. Disable the existing remote-management settings and confirm that the entry point is hidden.
3. Inspect the `PartialUnavailable`, `PartialDisconnectedRemotes`, and `NarrowPartialDisconnectedRemotes` Automations component fixtures in dark, light, and high-contrast themes as applicable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the Automations view with disconnected providers, both with saved automations (partial banner) and without saved automations (unavailable empty state).
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Widget construction creates two Link instances and two autoruns; catalogue/provider publication then performs two visibility checks and updates display styles. No asynchronous or external operation must complete before the warning renders.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two O(P) scans where P is the effective number of unavailable session providers; link/DOM/listener cardinality remains constant at two per Automations view.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous on the UI thread; exactly two independent autoruns, one for each persistent link location, with no queue or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The links and autoruns are constructed once per view instance and reused across state changes. The provider aggregate is an observable-derived value; there is no miss/retry or negative-cache behavior added by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed constructor calls renderManageRemotesLink exactly twice, each autorun scans unavailableProviders once and performs one display write, and all resources are registered on the disposable section.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of registered providers varies, but it is bounded by the small set of session providers rather than automations or history rows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added eager work is constant except for two small provider scans, performs no geometry reads or forced layout, and is disposed with the single custom-view widget.

Scenarios.Scenario: React to catalogue availability, disconnected-provider, or configuration changes while the Automations view remains open.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each relevant observable update, and any global configuration event, reruns both link visibility autoruns; each reads catalogue state, scans providers until a disconnected entry is found, reads up to three settings, and writes display only. This is not on input, scroll, animation, or frame-driven paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is 2 × O(P) per catalogue/provider/configuration event, with P equal to unavailable providers after provider aggregation; it does not scale with automation cards, run history, or view lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates execute synchronously under the observable scheduler; there are two subscribers and no asynchronous overlap. Configuration events are not batched by this diff, but realistic setting changes are infrequent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Visibility is recomputed rather than cached, while the Link objects themselves remain stable. There are no repeated external reads, retry loops, or retained per-event entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both observableSignalFromEvent instances are owned by AutomationCardsSection, both autoruns are registered, and the only scaling operation is Array.some over unavailable providers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository-wide configuration events can originate from many settings, but they are not a high-frequency product path and each changed run is bounded to constant work plus O(P).
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The duplicated bounded checks do not establish realistic CPU, rendering, or memory degradation, and listener cleanup follows the widget lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate Manage Remotes from an unavailable Automations warning.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click/Enter/Space handler issues one OPEN_REMOTES_EDITOR command and awaits the existing editor-open operation. On a cold editor open, RemotesModel construction starts tunnel-status loading and RemotesWidget visibility starts remote discovery without awaiting it, so discovery is off the editor-open critical path; the editor can render its busy state first.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request SSH config hosts from the main-process SSH service, which reads host configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per cold/open visibility refresh, independent of the number of disconnected providers shown in Automations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Automations warning had no direct route; invoking the same pre-existing Manage Remote Environments command from the Command Palette, Sessions menu, title bar, or environment picker performed the identical request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in the background refresh after the editor becomes visible and does not block the Automations link handler from opening the editor UI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On Windows, request WSL distribution discovery from the main-process service, transitively invoking the existing WSL discovery implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per refresh on Windows; zero on other operating systems.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent existing editor entry points triggered the same one-per-refresh WSL discovery; the diff only adds another user-selected entry point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs concurrently in the background and is not awaited by RemotesWidget.setVisible or the Automations command handler.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a silent tunnel authentication provider and list the account's dev tunnels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One tunnel listing sequence per refresh, not per provider, automation, or table row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing Remote Environments editor already performed this sequence whenever opened through its other commands or made visible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs concurrently with other discovery after the editor is visible; the table exposes refresh progress rather than blocking editor creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh GitHub environment data when that service is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one environment refresh per editor refresh, independent of displayed provider count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was already part of every equivalent Remote Environments refresh; the new Automations link does not increase calls within one open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs concurrently and off the command's editor-open critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the existing remote tunnel hosting status during cold RemotesModel construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per newly constructed editor model; the singleton editor/input reuses the model while open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold opens through all existing Remote Environments entry points constructed the same model and made the same status read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget initialization updates the model later and does not block editor opening.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Boundary count is bounded by remote kinds (up to four discovery operations plus one cold status read), not by disconnected provider labels, automations, or history size; result processing scales with discovered remotes as it did before the PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single activation maps to one command. The existing RemotesWidget cancels/replaces an earlier refresh, while RemotesModel fans out at most one discovery per kind (SSH, WSL on Windows, tunnels, and GitHub environments) via Promise.all. The singleton editor input avoids duplicate editor instances.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold open constructs the singleton editor/model and starts discovery. Reopening an already active singleton does not create another model; making an existing editor visible uses the editor's existing refresh semantics. A new refresh cancels and replaces the previous request rather than retaining unbounded work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: Link emits one opener callback per activation; the command opens a singleton RemotesEditorInput; RemotesWidget.setVisible starts one cancellable refresh whose four discovery kinds are grouped in one Promise.all.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual duration depends on SSH configuration, Windows/WSL availability, authentication, and network latency, but cardinality and off-critical-path scheduling are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The boundary fan-out belongs to the explicitly requested existing editor feature, is neither eager on Automations rendering nor multiplied by provider count, and an equivalent pre-diff editor open incurred the same work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Automations accessibility help after the added guidance text.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessible help content assembly includes one additional localized constant string when help is requested; no remote discovery or command execution occurs.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work and bytes, independent of providers, automations, and history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, single invocation per help request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes; the extra string is allocated with the existing help content on demand and released with that content.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff only appends one localize result to the content array.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the addition is a fixed-size string.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the fixed on-demand allocation is negligible and does not change boundary activity.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and traced view construction, observable updates, disposal, command routing, editor reuse, and transitive remote-discovery boundaries. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, so no findings were submitted.
